title: O mercado de comida
grammarPoint: Countable and uncountable nouns; much / many / a lot of

text.title: A Morning at a Market in Mexico City
paragraphs: Yesterday, I visited a big food market in Mexico City. There were a lot of people and a lot of noise, but I loved every minute.
There are many [[stalls]] with fresh fruit: mangoes, papayas and some fruits I didn't know. I bought a few mangoes and a little [[honey]] for my hotel room.
I wanted to try everything, but I didn't have much money, and I didn't have much time. So I asked a [[vendor]]: "How much are these tacos?" "Twenty pesos for three," she said. Very cheap!
How many tacos did I eat? Too many! The salsa had a lot of [[chili]], so I drank a lot of water. My friend doesn't eat much meat, so she had [[quesadillas]] with cheese and mushrooms.
My tip: go early. In the afternoon, there isn't much space to walk, and the best stalls don't have many tacos [[left]].

vendor.pt: vendedor, vendedora (de rua ou de feira)

quesadillas.note: Tortilhas dobradas e recheadas com queijo, típicas do México.

left.note: "There aren't many tacos left" = "não sobraram muitos tacos".

grammar.title: Contáveis e incontáveis: much, many, a lot of
explanation: Em inglês, alguns substantivos são contáveis: podemos contar (one mango, two mangoes, many stalls). Outros são incontáveis: não têm plural e não usam a ou an (water, money, time, honey, meat, noise).

Many vem com contáveis no plural (many stalls, many tacos). Much vem com incontáveis (much money, much time). Na prática, much e many aparecem mais em frases negativas e perguntas: I didn't have much money.
A lot of funciona com os dois e é o mais usado em frases afirmativas: a lot of people, a lot of water.
Para perguntar quantidade: How many + contável (How many tacos?) e How much + incontável (How much time?). How much também pergunta o preço: How much are these tacos?
Para "alguns" ou "um pouco": a few + contável (a few mangoes) e a little + incontável (a little honey). Para "demais": too many e too much.
Cuidado: algumas palavras são contáveis em português e incontáveis em inglês. Information, advice e furniture nunca vão para o plural: some information, e não informations.

examples.en: There are many stalls with fresh fruit.
examples.pt: Tem muitas barracas com frutas frescas.

examples.en: I bought a few mangoes and a little honey.
examples.pt: Comprei algumas mangas e um pouco de mel.

exercises.prompt: O que a autora comprou para o quarto do hotel?
options: Algumas mangas e um pouco de mel
exercises.explanation: O texto diz: "I bought a few mangoes and a little honey for my hotel room."

exercises.statement: The author had a lot of money at the market.

exercises.explanation: A vendedora diz: "Twenty pesos for three".

exercises.statement: The author's friend doesn't eat much meat.
exercises.explanation: Verdadeiro: "My friend doesn't eat much meat, so she had quesadillas".

exercises.sentence: There are ___ stalls with fresh fruit.
exercises.explanation: Stalls é contável e está no plural, então usamos many.
Time é incontável, então usamos much.
Tacos é contável (one taco, two tacos): How many tacos?

options: Can you give me some information?
Can you give me some informations?
Can you give me an information?
exercises.explanation: Information é incontável em inglês: não tem plural e não usa an. Use some information.

exercises.prompt: Coloque as palavras na ordem certa.
exercises.explanation: A few com contáveis (mangoes) e a little com incontáveis (honey).
